gloss: to be the first to speak; to start things off

definitions.gloss: to be the first to speak; to start things off; to break the ice
definitions.explanation: To be the one who initiates a discussion, debate, or action. Often used when someone is the first to speak up or take action in a group setting.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}が{議論|ぎろん}の{口火|くちび}を{切|き}った。
{誰|だれ}も{発言|はつげん}しないので、{私|わたし}が{口火|くちび}を{切|き}ることにした。
examples.english: Since nobody was speaking up, I decided to start things off.

examples.japanese: {反対|はんたい}{派|は}の{代表|だいひょう}が{口火|くちび}を{切|き}り、{次|つぎ}々と{意見|いけん}が{出|で}された。
examples.english: The representative of the opposition started things off, and opinions poured out one after another.

notes:
Originally a military term: {口火|くちび} refers to the fuse or primer of a firearm, so {口火|くちび}を{切|き}る literally meant 'to light the fuse' or 'to open fire.' Now used figuratively to mean being the first to speak or act, triggering a chain of events.

ETYMOLOGY:
{口火|くちび} is the opening of a furnace or the touch hole of a cannon — the small ignition point that sets off the main charge. The metaphor extends to being the catalyst that sets a discussion or movement in motion.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {議論|ぎろん}の{口火|くちび}を{切|き}る — to kick off a debate
- {批判|ひはん}の{口火|くちび}を{切|き}る — to be the first to criticize
- {改革|かいかく}の{口火|くちび}を{切|き}る — to spark reform

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {先陣|せんじん}を{切|き}る — to take the lead, to be at the vanguard; broader in scope, not limited to speech
- {火蓋|ひぶた}を{切|き}る — to open hostilities; similar military origin, often used for the start of a battle or fierce competition
